correctness.rationale: The codimension-one linear-map Jacobian gives section volume κ_(d−1) det(A)/sqrt(sum a_i² U_i²), hence its normalized inverse square is a positive spherical quadratic form with spectrum b_i. Squared Haar coordinates are Dirichlet(1/2,...,1/2), giving G(z)=prod(1-b_i z)^(-1/2). The first d moments determine the degree-d polynomial G(z)^(-2), whose positive roots reconstruct the axes for all multiplicities. With known volume its constant coefficient is given so d-1 moments suffice. At simple positive spectra the polynomial coefficients can be perturbed independently to show locally matching first d-1, or at fixed determinant d-2, moments with noncongruent axes. Exact rational verifier checked degrees 2–5, a planar ambiguous pair, and independently restricted 3D section quadratic forms; finite tests are not an infinite proof.

value.rationale: The classical geometric tomography question loses section orientations, and the available full distribution carries strictly less information than a labeled section function. For the canonical full ellipsoid class, the theorem establishes an exact optimal initial-population-moment budget for complete congruence-class determination, with a sharp known-volume refinement and generic impossibility at the next lower cutoff. This is a natural complete finite-data identifiability invariant with potential for stereological calibration; it is not merely a known density or a single special numerical evaluation. It does not promise statistical stability, novel general-body uniqueness, or external certification.
